gap: No result ChatGPT got states that its 'best overall value' pick, the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5X, lasted 42 h 10 min in SoundGuys' test over the 2.4 GHz dongle at about 50% volume. That is below the 50 h SteelSeries rates for the dongle, well below the '60-hour' figure ChatGPT showed (the Bluetooth rating), and about half the 83 to 85 h that SoundGuys and RTINGS measured on the cheaper Turtle Beach Stealth 600 Gen 3.
standout_why: I read the cited RTINGS page (updated 2026-11-04) through a text proxy, because it loads with JavaScript. It gives the Stealth 600 Gen 3 '85 hours per charge', the original Arctis Nova 7X 'over 33 hours', and the BlackShark V3 Pro 13 ms latency. It does not mention the Arctis Nova 5X. It lists the Xbox Wireless Headset only as a notable mention with no hour figure. I could not read the cited Tom's Guide list: the direct fetch returned only navigation and the proxy returned HTTP 403. So the Stealth figure is already partly covered by a rival. A measured runtime for the Nova 5X, side by side with the others, is not on any page I could read.
decides: This supports the Stealth 600 Gen 3 as the wireless pick when battery matters. Two outlets measured it at 83 h 42 min and 85 h, and the maker sells it for $109.99 against $149.99 for the Nova 5X, which measured 42 h 10 min. Our page also needs a fix: its Xbox Wireless Headset row pairs Microsoft's 2024 claim of 20 h with SoundGuys' 19 h 18 min, but that test was of the original 2021 model (rated 15 h, Bluetooth 4.2). The tested value for the 2024 model should be dropped until someone measures it. The Stealth figures also need a note on which version was tested: SoundGuys tested the PC/PlayStation version and RTINGS tested the Xbox version.

findings.label: Measured continuous battery life, 2.4 GHz USB-C dongle
findings.source_title: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5X review: One gaming headset to rule them all? - SoundGuys (Adam Birney, updated 2025-03-28, first published 2024-07-17)
findings.note: SoundGuys tested on a PC over the USB-C dongle at about 50% volume. The article says '2.5 GHz', which looks like a typo for 2.4 GHz. SteelSeries rates 50 h on the dongle and 60 h on Bluetooth, so ChatGPT's '60-hour' figure is the Bluetooth rating. The measurement is 84% of the 50 h dongle rating.
